A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRIM study. All 27 pages of v2 and 28 pages of v3, including Appendices A–N, are readable. Text, equations, tables and all six figures support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning evaluations, selection runtimes, transfer experiments, ablations and robustness analyses in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds layer-group and saliency-weight ablation results in Appendix H.

M1.justification: v3 adds coverage to the main scoring equation and Algorithm 2, bringing them into agreement with the rule already defined in v2 Appendix C, Equation (15), and the default configuration in Appendix H. The complete documented method does not gain a new component.

E1.justification: The instruction pools, MathInstruct setting and all main-text and appendix benchmarks are retained. The new ablations use already-covered MMLU and GSM8K tasks without introducing different populations or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Random, BM25, DSIR, S2L, RDS, CLD, LESS, TAGCOS and the transfer/oracle comparisons where previously evaluated. The new ablations compare TRIM configurations.

E3.justification: New Appendix H experiments compare early, middle and last groups of six layers and sweep seven row/column saliency-weight pairs. These add controlled experimental settings; existing splits, training budgets, defaults, metrics and prompting protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's final-layer-count ablation, v3 adds tests of layer position and the balance between row and column saliency (H.2–H.3, Tables 10–11). Existing pooling, IDF, fallback, checkpoint, robustness and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Table 11 reports saliency-weight accuracies without standard deviations, unlike the existing ablation tables and new Table 10. Appendix H retains its three-seed mean/standard-deviation convention. This is a limited difference in uncertainty reporting; no changed run count is established.

E6.justification: New Table 10 reports GSM8K accuracies of 20.34%, 24.23% and 29.52% for early, middle and last six layers. Table 11 adds MMLU saliency-weight results ranging from 47.24% to 49.33%. Matched pre-existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mean, maximum and coverage definitions displayed in v3 Equations (13)–(16) already appear in v2 Appendix C. The mathematical reasoning and computational-cost analysis are retained, with no new assumptions, proofs or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: efficient forward-only token-level selection, up to 9% downstream gains, surpassing full-data tuning in some settings, transferability and in-domain selection without separate target examples.

C2.justification: New H.2 interprets the layer-group results as supporting upper-layer representations tied to prediction and decision-making. H.3 interprets the weight sweep as supporting balanced or near-balanced saliency. Existing interpretations and applicability qualifications are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit TRIM code-availability link in its first-page footnote. Existing training, hardware and software details remain unchanged. The coverage coefficient and scoring rule clarified elsewhere in v3 were already documented in v2's appendices.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gao et al. (2024), Higher Layers Need More LoRA Experts, and Liu et al. (2024c), Fantastic Semantics and Where to Find Them, to motivate layer choice. Other citation changes update existing works or the same evaluation-harness artifact; overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 locally expands the scoring explanation and Appendix H, adds acknowledgements, and replaces the preprint footer with conference-proceedings information. The main section order and Appendices A–N remain intact, with limited rewriting elsewhere.

P2.justification: v3 adds appendix Tables 10–11 and renumbers subsequent tables. Existing floats are redistributed, including Tables 3–4 moving from page 7 to page 8. All six figure contents are retained; the presentation changes are localized additions and reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the mismatch between the main scoring equation/pseudocode and v2's existing appendix coverage rule. The two new ablations strengthen support for retained design choices, and the code link improves access information. These are limited quality gains: principal results and claims remain unchanged, and new Table 11 lacks standard deviations.
